title: Visiting Hours: Night 1, Larch Street on a hill
subtitle: Layout A's four routes laid on a slope, as you offered: Walt's bike shop at the bottom by the creek, the house with its tower at the top, four terraces 12 m apart. The plan first, then the stills from the bottom, the middle and the top (from the run of 2026-10-12, before the fixes listed below).
questions: Does the hill show the size of the setting? From the far bank you see the whole climb; from the lookout at the top you see the whole street.

Keep the gold beacon? The tower alone is hidden from most of the climb (you walk under 12 m retaining walls), so a soft column of light stands up out of it: with it the house is found from 74 to 100% of every route. Without it, the tower shows from 0 to 18% of the way.

Is any route too long or too short? The road takes about 32 s (two switchbacks, 308 m), the garden stairs 10 s, the rooftops 12 s (nine double jumps), the creek ravine 30 s (the culvert slide, 28 falls). The way in, from the arrival over the creek and through the shop to Walt, takes about 4 s.
notes: Fixed after these stills, not shown yet: the flood wall along the creek is drawn 1.2 m high now (it hid the foot of the hill from the far bank) and the dream holds it at 5 m; the world's edges have walls and hedges (there was sky under the hill past them); the hedge on the far bank replaces a white 6 m fence; the middle, rooftop and ravine cameras moved to where the view is.
Both halves of Walt's optional premise ('the same Saturday') are below his gate: the neighbours' loop plays on the far bank where you arrive, and Saturday's paper is on his yard bench.
Every line is a placeholder. Elias is a stand-in figure (there's no art of him yet); the shop's sign has no lettering.
